prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-04-23. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.39 |
| Retained earnings       | 0M |
| Current liabilities     | 22,085M |
| Current assets          | 30,590M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 21,312M |
| Total liabilities       | 52,676M |
| Total assets            | 73,988M |
| EBIT / operating income | 886M |
| Revenue                 | 9,143M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-04-23, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported balance sheet shows high leverage (equity only ~29% of total assets) with zero retained earnings, implying limited loss-absorption capacity and no demonstrated earnings retention. Liquidity is only adequate (current ratio 1.39) and EBIT margins are modest (~9.7%), which together are consistent with a non-investment-grade profile but not yet near-term default risk.
DECISION: BB
(The data are insufficient for finer notches within the BB band.)
